frequency_question: How often is a major transboundary water treaty successfully renewed or replaced with a successor agreement prior to or immediately upon the expiration of its multi-decade predecessor term?
membership_rule: Members are formal bilateral treaties governing shared river basins with fixed multi-decade durations that reached their expiration point. Excluded are informal understandings or unilateral actions without treaty status.
window: Within a 3-year window leading up to or immediately following the expiration date

cases.name: 1960 Indus Waters Treaty (perpetual, but operational renewals)
1997 UN Watercourses Convention ratification context (general baseline)

provenance_note: claims 18 cases from only 4 named (4.5x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 18 named instances; believed roughly 20 in total globally
known_gaps: Excludes minor bilateral agreements between sub-national entities or non-ratified drafts.
skeleton: Total major bilateral transboundary water treaties reaching 30-year milestone mark since 1950
multiplier: 15 historical renewal instances observed across major river basins / 18 total eligible treaty milestones
validity_reason: Global state practice on transboundary water governance changes slowly over decades.
